title: Mental health of refugees and migrants: risk and protective factors and access to care (2023)
note: Evidence review covering diverse migrant and refugee populations. Used for determinants and barriers to care, not an African diaspora prevalence estimate.

title: Do international migrants increase their happiness and that of their families by migrating? World Happiness Report 2018, chapter 3
note: Gallup World Poll analysis with over 36,000 first-generation migrants from over 150 countries and territories. Matching is observational; +0.47 is a life-evaluation point difference on a 0-10 scale, not a forecast or African-only effect.

title: Migration and mental health: evidence from a natural experiment (2009)
note: Journal of Health Economics 28(3):677-687. Tonga-New Zealand migration ballot study found mental-health improvements. The route, population and outcome differ from this report’s audience.

title: Indicators of Immigrant Integration 2023, section 3.12: Overqualification
note: About one-third of highly educated employed immigrants in the OECD and EU were overqualified. The definition concerns job skill level, not personal ability. Reporting years vary; this is not a 2026 African-only measure.

organisation: European Union Agency for Fundamental Rights
title: Being Black in the EU: experiences of people of African descent (2023)
note: 2022 survey; almost 6,800 people of sub-Saharan African origin in 13 EU countries, including immigrants and descendants. 34% reported racial discrimination in the prior 12 months. Not all Africans, destinations or newcomers.

title: Social isolation and loneliness / Commission on Social Connection (2025)
note: WHO reports approximately 16%, or one in six, experiencing loneliness worldwide. Global context only; not a migrant-specific or African-specific estimate.

title: An exploration of the relational well-being of African international students at a South African university (2024)
note: South African Journal of Higher Education 38(4). Qualitative interviews with 16 students at one university; five women, eleven men, mean age 24. Findings describe experiences, not prevalence.

title: From struggle to strength in African and Middle Eastern newcomers’ integration stories to Canada (2024)
note: PLOS ONE. Participatory qualitative study of 18 newcomers aged 18-30 in Ontario; 78% female, around half post-secondary students. Includes different migration categories; not nationally representative.

title: Is everywhere I go home? Reflections on the acculturation journey of African international students in China (2025)
note: International Journal of Intercultural Relations 105, 102136. Qualitative study of 15 students at three research-intensive universities, in China for 4-7 years. An institutional repository copy of the research paper.

title: Emotional connectedness to home for Ghanaian students in the UK (2014)
note: British Journal of Guidance & Counselling 42(4):383-402. Two focus groups involving nine Ghanaian students; narrative analysis of belonging and separation.

title: An interpretive phenomenological analysis of the help-seeking behaviours and coping strategies of male Nigerian international students
note: Doctoral qualitative research with eight male Nigerian international students at a UK university. Themes included coping, service barriers, African identity and masculinity; not a statement about all African men.

title: The U-curve on trial: a longitudinal study of psychological and sociocultural adjustment during cross-cultural transition (1998)
note: International Journal of Intercultural Relations 22(3):277-291. Followed 35 Japanese students in New Zealand at four points through 12 months; neither adjustment measure followed the proposed U-curve. A counterexample, not an African recovery timetable.

title: Mental health at work
note: Official guidance, checked October 2026. Addresses job insecurity, excessive demands, discrimination, working conditions and organizational responses. No workforce prevalence figure is extrapolated to African migrants.

title: General principles and operational guidelines for fair recruitment and definition of recruitment fees and related costs (2019)
note: International guidance includes the principle that workers should not bear recruitment fees or related costs. It is not a guarantee about enforcement or a statement of each country’s domestic law.

title: Depressive disorder (depression)
note: Official information on symptoms, duration, effective treatment and help-seeking, checked October 2026. Used for general health information, not diagnosis.

title: Doing What Matters in Times of Stress: an illustrated guide (2020)
note: Public stress-management resource with language and audio options. Self-help can complement appropriate care; the report does not reproduce its exercises.

title: Reintegration Counselling: A Psychosocial Approach (2019)
note: Professional guidance on psychosocial aspects of return and reintegration. Used to support planning for return, not to predict an individual’s experience.

title: World report on the health of refugees and migrants (2022)
note: Discusses legal, financial, linguistic and administrative barriers to health. Refugee experiences and voluntary study or work migration are not treated as interchangeable.

organisation: UK Council for International Student Affairs
title: Culture shock for international students
note: Practical student guidance on adjustment and support. Specific to a UK student context; no universal adjustment schedule is inferred.
